entry.title: Platja de Roses
entry.summary: Roses sits on a big, sweeping bay at the top of the Costa Brava, with a long beach of fine sand and calm water. The Cap de Creus natural park and the small cove of Canyelles are a short drive away.

entry.title: Praia da Povoa de Varzim
entry.summary: Povoa de Varzim has a wide, flat beach of golden sand on the Atlantic coast north of Porto, with a casino, promenade and fishing quarter behind. The sea is cool and waves are moderate, so beaches are usually staffed by lifeguards.

entry.title: Plage de Saint-Aygulf, Frejus
entry.summary: Saint-Aygulf is a long, family-friendly sand beach near Frejus, with clear shallow water and a backdrop of pines and the red Esterel hills. It is quieter than Saint-Raphael and Frejus plage.

entry.title: Playa de Moraira
entry.summary: Moraira is a small, upmarket town on the Costa Blanca with a calm sandy cove and an old fishing quarter. The water is clear and sheltered, and the cliff paths lead to small rocky coves nearby.

entry.title: Hersonissos Beach
entry.summary: Hersonissos has a sandy town beach and many smaller coves along the north coast of Crete, with warm clear water and a lively promenade. Mountains rise behind, and the old town of Piskopiano is a short drive up the hill.

entry.title: Praia da Costa da Caparica
entry.summary: Costa da Caparica is a long stretch of wide Atlantic beach just across the river from Lisbon, with fine sand, big waves and beach bars. The nearby Fossil Cliffs and the small tourist train make it an easy day trip.

entry.title: Porec Beach
entry.summary: Porec has stone platforms, pebbles and small concrete lidos around its old town, with clear and calm Adriatic water. The Euphrasian Basilica is a World Heritage site, and the beaches on the Brulo and Plava Laguna sides are easy to reach.

entry.title: Sidari Beach
entry.summary: Sidari on the north coast of Corfu has sandy beaches and a maze of golden sandstone cliffs carved by the sea. The famous Canal d Amour is a narrow channel where visitors swim and take photos.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Punta Ala
entry.summary: Punta Ala is a quiet resort in the Tuscan Maremma, with a wide sandy beach edged by pine woods and a small marina. The water is clear and the area is calm, with views toward the island of Elba on a clear day.

entry.title: Plage de Cabourg
entry.summary: Cabourg is a belle epoque seaside town on the Normandy coast, with a very wide beach of fine sand and an iconic promenade lined with colourful cabins. The tide goes out far, and the grand hotel was a favourite of the writer Proust.

entry.title: Plage de Cavaliere, Le Lavandou
entry.summary: Cavaliere is a long, wide beach of fine sand west of Le Lavandou, backed by pines and facing the Iles d Or. The water is clear and shallow, and boats leave from Le Lavandou for Porquerolles and Port-Cros.

entry.title: Plage de Collioure
entry.summary: Collioure is a painters town on the Vermilion Coast, with small pebble beaches on either side of a royal castle and a bell tower on the water. The sea is clear and calm, and the harbour is full of coloured boats.

entry.title: Plage du Touquet
entry.summary: Le Touquet-Paris-Plage has a huge beach of fine sand, backed by dunes and pine woods, on the Opal Coast. The sea is cool, the tides are wide, and the town has Belle Epoque villas and sand yachting.

entry.title: Playa San Cristobal, Almunecar
entry.summary: Playa San Cristobal is a long beach of dark pebbles and coarse sand below the Almunecar old town, with a medieval castle on the rock above. The sea is clear and steep, and the Costa Tropical is known for subtropical fruit and mild winters.

entry.title: Playa de la Rada, Estepona
entry.summary: Playa de la Rada is the main beach of Estepona, a wide, gently shelving strip of dark sand and fine pebbles with a palm-lined promenade. The old town behind is known for its flower-filled streets and murals.

entry.title: Platja del Regueral, Cambrils
entry.summary: Platja del Regueral is a long, quiet beach of sand and fine gravel near Cambrils, a fishing town known for its seafood. The sea is calm and the beach has a lower-key feel than neighbouring Salou.

entry.title: Platja de Salou
entry.summary: Salou is a family resort on the Costa Dorada, with a long beach of fine sand and calm shallow water. The promenade has bars, restaurants and activities, and PortAventura is a short ride away.

entry.title: Platja de Blanes
entry.summary: Blanes is the southern gateway to the Costa Brava, with a long beach of coarse golden sand and a green headland behind. The old town and the Marimurtra botanical garden are close by.

entry.title: Platja de Calella de Palafrugell
entry.summary: Calella de Palafrugell is a charming fishing village with small sand and pebble coves between rocks, backed by white arcades. The water is clear, and the coastal path leads to larger coves like Llafranc and Tamariu.

entry.title: Platja de Cadaques
entry.summary: Cadaques is a whitewashed fishing village at the far northeast of the Costa Brava, with a small pebble and sand beach on a sheltered bay. The water is clear and the village is famous as the home town of the painter Dali and an artists retreat.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Finale Ligure
entry.summary: Finale Ligure has a long beach of sand and fine pebbles below the white limestone cliffs of the Ligurian hills. The water is clear, the town is pastel and easy to walk, and the area is also a famed rock climbing and hiking base.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Caorle
entry.summary: Caorle is an old fishing town on the Veneto coast with a long beach of fine pale sand and warm shallow water. The historic centre has coloured houses, a round-topped bell tower and a small sanctuary on the rocks.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Cattolica
entry.summary: Cattolica is a classic Romagna beach resort, with a very wide strip of fine sand and warm shallow water. It suits families and has a long promenade with plenty of bars and restaurants.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Giardini Naxos
entry.summary: Giardini Naxos is a bay of grey pebbles and warm clear water at the foot of Taormina, with Mount Etna smoking in the distance. The seafront has bars and bathing clubs, and Isola Bella is a short drive north.

entry.title: Spiaggia di Levante, Terracina
entry.summary: Terracina has a long beach of fine sand on the Lazio coast, with the rocky bulk of Monte Sant Angelo rising above the town. The water is clear and shelves gently, and the upper old town is a short drive away.

entry.title: Playa de Benicassim
entry.summary: Benicassim has a long strip of golden sand and pebbles on the Orange Blossom Coast, backed by a promenade of old villas. The water is calm and shallow, and the coast is known for its summer music festival.

entry.title: Bibione Beach
entry.summary: Bibione has a wide beach of fine sand stretching along the Adriatic coast between the Tagliamento and Livenza rivers. The water is shallow and warm, and rows of umbrellas line the shore.

entry.title: Durres Beach
entry.summary: Durres has a long beach of grey sand along the Adriatic coast, close to Albania largest port and the ruins of the Roman amphitheatre. The water is warm and shallow, and the promenade is lively in summer.

entry.title: Praia da Vagueira
entry.summary: Praia da Vagueira is a long, wide Atlantic beach of golden sand backed by dunes, near the lagoon of Aveiro. It is quieter than the better known beaches of the Algarve, with strong waves that suit surfers.

entry.title: Praia da Figueira da Foz
entry.summary: The beach of Figueira da Foz is famously wide, with a long stretch of fine golden sand beside the mouth of the Mondego river. Atlantic waves roll in, and the city promenade is just behind.
